answer: Make each identity keep its own 8 GB memory-hard table in RAM, expanded from its key so no two keys can share one. Each epoch a verifier sends a seed for a voyage of 100,000 dependent lookups; each 64-byte cell names the next address, so nothing can be fetched ahead. The final hash plus Merkle proofs for 16 random steps is due in 1 second: RAM takes about 10 ms, SSD paging about 8 s. One agent pays roughly $25 a month; 1,000 clones need 8 TB, about $25,000. A farm packing many keys into one orchard of ferrous racks runs short of memory, misses deadlines and loses those seats.
